pages.text: $(italic)From an ORSA orbital geology brief.$()$(br2)The ice sheet loads the crust. Along old geothermal seams, that pressure forces hot brine, steam and sulfur melt back to the surface.
Satellites saw new heat blooms most often under snow belts, taiga and glacial basins.

pages.title: Vent Classes
pages.text: $(bold)Dormant:$() mineral basin, faint bleed, no shelter value.$(br)$(bold)Warm:$() brief warmth once Phase 6 begins.$(br)$(bold)Active:$() stable heat pocket, geyser bursts.$(br)$(bold)Rupture:$() growing cone, sulfur lava, ejecta, ashfall.$(br2)Natural ground features, not structures.

pages.title: Field Guidance
pages.text: $(li)Warm vents: temporary refuge$(li)Active vents: risky shelter$(li)Rupture vents: landmarks to survive around, not on$(br2)A $(l:orsa_equipment/surveyor_lens)Surveyor Lens$(/l) sees only exposed heat, steam and hot crust. Buried vents stay hidden until the ground opens.

Mature rupture mouths carry sulfur crust, friable tuff and heavy yellow deposits. The basin interior was too unstable for routine extraction.$(br2)If the ground vibrates in vacuum, the pressure column is about to move.
